description: Packet Hacking Village explores network packet analysis, cyberpsychological active defense, open-source intelligence pipelines, visual threat modeling, and local malware triage environments.

talks.title: Pwning the Pwners with Mindware
talks.teaser: Frank DiGiovanni leverages cyberpsychology and the DoD's Tularosa Study to target human adversary cognition, shifting defensive operations into active deception.
talks.summary:
Reversing the Asymmetry of Cyber Defense

Traditional cyber defense operates at a disadvantage, reacting to adversary actions while attackers iterate freely across corporate perimeters.

The Principles of Cyberpsychology and Cognitive Deception

Drawing upon the Department of Defense's 'Tularosa Study', Frank DiGiovanni explores how cognitive psychology and artificial intelligence can manipulate an attacker's perception and decision-making.

Targeting the Human Operator in the Kill Chain

By injecting deceptive telemetry, artificial delays, and confusing system architectures, defenders induce cognitive fatigue, doubt, and operational errors in human adversaries.

Operational Vignettes and Active Defense Frameworks

The author details concrete operational scenarios, demonstrating how active psychological deception transforms defensive monitoring into proactive threat neutralization.

talks.title: OSINT for Physical Security Intelligence
talks.teaser: Demonstrates automated OSINT collection pipelines to extract actionable physical security intelligence, predictive indicators, and geopolitical risk assessments.
talks.summary:
Transforming Open Source Information into Actionable Intelligence

Organizations frequently waste hours sifting through uncurated open-source data streams without extracting actionable intelligence during critical physical security events.

Automating Curated Data Ingestion Pipelines

The speakers demonstrate automated filtering architectures that eliminate 99% of preliminary analysis time, distilling social media and geospatial signals into high-confidence feeds.

Predictive Analysis for Natural Disasters and Geopolitical Crises

Correlating multi-source open-source intelligence enables predictive threat modeling for facility safety, supply chain disruptions, and emerging regional conflicts.

Frameworks for Physical Security Intelligence Operations

The presentation provides practical operational blueprints for integrating automated OSINT streams into corporate security operation centers.

talks.title: WINE Pairing with Malware
talks.teaser: Jared Stroud configures WINE and Valve Proton gaming compatibility layers on Linux as lightweight, local malware analysis sandboxes to extract IoCs.
talks.summary:
Repurposing Gaming Compatibility Layers for Malware Analysis

The rapid evolution of WINE and Proton for running modern Windows video games on Linux provides a robust runtime environment capable of executing Windows PE malware.

Configuring Lightweight Linux Triage Environments

Jared Stroud demonstrates setting up headless WINE environments on Linux to execute unknown malware samples without expensive commercial sandbox infrastructure.

Extracting IoCs Using Native UNIX Utilities

Leveraging standard command-line tools like awk, grep, strace, and network packet capture utilities enables rapid extraction of forensic indicators and C2 network endpoints.

Accelerating Offense-Defense Iteration Cycles

The presentation illustrates how malware authors and defensive analysts can use WINE environments to rapidly test implants, validate evasion techniques, and shorten feedback loops.

talks.title: The Importance of Arts and Crafts in ThreatOps
talks.teaser: Pete Hay presents visual diagramming frameworks to communicate complex threat intelligence, incident timelines, and multi-stage attack graphs in ThreatOps.
talks.summary:
The Visual Communication Challenge in Incident Response

Cybersecurity analysts frequently struggle to convey complex multi-stage intrusions to non-technical executive stakeholders and cross-functional engineering teams.

Overcoming Divergent Threat Modeling Diagrams

Pete Hay identifies that asking multiple analysts to map the same incident yields conflicting, disorganized diagrams that obscure critical attack paths.

Standardizing ThreatOps Visual Frameworks

The presentation introduces structured visual templates for diagramming adversary campaigns, Kill Chain stages, lateral movement pivots, and infrastructure clusters.

Enhancing Incident Reporting and Decision-Making

High-density, visually intuitive diagrams accelerate executive incident decision-making and improve operational coordination across detection and response teams.

talks.title: Death by 1000 Likes: The Online Wall of Sheep
talks.teaser: Will Kay details building an automated OSINT scraper for Reddit to monitor year-round credential leaks, creating a virtual Wall of Sheep.
talks.summary:
Extending the Wall of Sheep Beyond DEF CON

Inspired by DEF CON's famous Packet Hacking Village Wall of Sheep, which displays credentials broadcast over unencrypted convention Wi-Fi, Australian researchers expanded the concept online.

Scraping Social Media for Accidental Information Leaks

Will Kay details developing automated scraping pipelines targeting the r/defcon subreddit and hacker forums between DEF CON 30 and 31.

Analyzing Year-Round Credential and Data Exposure

Aggregating publicly shared photos, badge photos, QR codes, and forum posts reveals persistent operational security lapses among conference attendees year-round.

Lessons in Personal OPSEC and Social Media Hygiene

The presentation highlights how innocuous social media posts can be aggregated into detailed personal profiles, urging attendees to practice disciplined digital hygiene.
